title: REGLAT at ArGuard Shared Tasks: An Ensemble-Based Model Integrating NER for Harmful Content Detection in Arabic
abstract: arXiv:2610.37265v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Detecting harmful content in Arabic is challenging because of dialectal variations and the semantic overlap between different harm categories. This paper presents a two-stage approach for classifying Arabic user prompts into seven categories of harmful content. First, GLiNER is used to extract harm-related entities from each prompt. The extracted entities are then added to the original text and passed to a fine-tuned MARBERT classifier for final classification. The approach combines explicit entity information with the contextual understanding of a pretrained Arabic language model. The system was evaluated on the development set of the ArGuard 2026 shared task. The results achieved a macro-F1 score of 0.886 and an accuracy of 0.897, demonstrating promising performance in fine-grained harmful content detection. tldr: 本文提出一种两阶段方法：先利用 GLiNER 从阿拉伯语用户提示中提取危害相关实体，再将其并入原文输入微调的 MARBERT 分类器，从而实现对七类阿拉伯语有害内容的细粒度检测。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a two-stage approach that first uses GLiNER to extract harm-related entities from Arabic user prompts and then feeds them together with the original text into a fine-tuned MARBERT classifier, enabling fine-grained detection of seven categories of harmful Arabic content.
